_comment: 'bad' samples are competitor references the gate must catch. There is at
least one per declared competitor, and the self-test fails if a competitor
is declared without one — otherwise a name could be added to the config,
never exercised, and quietly stop matching.
'good' samples are real integration shapes taken from surfaces that exist
in this tree: a connector module docstring, a plugin manifest, a setup
guide, the connector registry, an imported detection rule's provenance
link, and the lower-case SEO keyword list. Flagging any of these would be
a false positive that breaks working connector code and documentation.
'comparison_bad' / 'comparison_good' exercise the narrower rule applied to
published comparison tables, where even an integration vendor's name is a
violation because the table's job is to position AiSOC against it.

bad.text: Where Cyble beats them: Prophet Security is a point product with no SOAR.
Dropzone AI focuses on fully automated first-line response.
Radiant Security — AI-powered SOC with alert correlation, Series A stage.
Commercial deployments at Intezer Analyze report Tier-1 parity.
microsoft security copilot adds natural-language SIEM querying.
Bundle threat: Security Copilot is free for top-tier suite customers.
Google Chronicle + Duet AI: strong for Google-native stacks.
Palo Alto XSIAM creates lock-in that AiSOC avoids.
Torq requires playbook authors; AiSOC requires none for standard cases.
Sales play: playbook fatigue — Torq/Tines customer displacement motion.
Swimlane / Tines: automation platforms, weak on AI reasoning depth.
